title: The Concept of Cognitive Dissonance
text:
Cognitive dissonance describes the mental discomfort experienced by an individual who holds two or more contradictory beliefs, ideas, or values, or is confronted by new information that conflicts with existing beliefs. This psychological state motivates individuals to reduce the inconsistency, often leading them to change their beliefs, alter their behaviors, or rationalize the conflict by adding consonant cognitions.

Research suggests that the magnitude of dissonance is proportional to the importance of the cognitions involved. For example, after investing significant effort into a belief or decision (effort justification), individuals tend to inflate the perceived value of that outcome to justify the initial commitment, even if objective evidence suggests otherwise. This mechanism highlights how internal consistency plays a vital role in maintaining psychological equilibrium.
